title: Histograms
summary: Learn how histogram bar area, class width and frequency density connect so you can complete tables and draw accurate bars.

items.prompt: A histogram uses the class interval $7 \le t < 15$. What is the class width?
items.explanation: Class width is the upper boundary minus the lower boundary: $15-7=8$.

items.prompt: For the class $2 \le t < 10$, the frequency is $24$. What is the frequency density?
items.explanation: Frequency density is $\dfrac{\text{frequency}}{\text{class width}}$. The width is $10-2=8$, so the density is $24\div8=3$.

items.prompt: A histogram bar covers $5 \le x < 13$ and has frequency density $1.5$. What frequency does the bar represent?
items.explanation: Frequency is the area of the bar: $\text{class width}\times\text{frequency density}$. Therefore, $(13-5)\times1.5=8\times1.5=12$.

items.prompt: The class $0 \le t < 4$ has frequency $18$, while the class $4 \le t < 10$ has frequency density $2$. What are the frequency density of the first class and the frequency of the second class?
items.explanation: For the first class, the density is $18\div4=4.5$. For the second class, the width is $10-4=6$, so the frequency is $6\times2=12$.

items.prompt: A histogram bar covers $20 \le m < 35$ and represents a frequency of $45$. Assuming values are evenly distributed within the class, estimate the frequency for $24 \le m < 30$.
items.explanation: The whole class has width $35-20=15$, so its density is $45\div15=3$. The interval from $24$ to $30$ has width $6$, giving an estimated frequency of $6\times3=18$.
